arxiv-2110-10720.title: Privacy in Open Search: A Review of Challenges and Solutions
arxiv-2110-10720.creator: Samuel Sousa 1, Roman Kern 1, Know-Center GmbH, Graz, Austria 1 also at ISDS, Graz University of Technology, Graz, Austria Christian Guetl, ISDS, Graz University of Technology, Graz, Austria
arxiv-2110-10720.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Samuel Sousa 1, Roman Kern 1, Know-Center GmbH, Graz, Austria 1 also at ISDS, Graz University of Technology, Graz, Austria Christian Guetl, ISDS, Graz University of Technology, Graz, Austria. Privacy is of worldwide concern regarding activities and processes that include sensitive data. For this reason, many countries and territories have been recently approving regulations controlling the extent to which organizations may exploit data provided by people.

arxiv-2110-11785.title: Double Proton Transfer in Hydrated Formic Acid Dimer: Interplay of Spatial Symmetry and Solvent-Generated Force on Reactivity
arxiv-2110-11785.creator: Kai Töpfer, Silvan Käser, Markus Meuwly
arxiv-2110-11785.description: Abstract The double proton transfer (DPT) reaction in hydrated formic acid dimer (FAD) is investigated at molecular-level detail. For this, a global and reactive machine learned (ML) potential energy surface (PES) is developed to run extensive (more than 100 ns) mixed ML/MM molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in explicit molecular mechanics (MM) solvent at MP2-quality for the solute.

arxiv-2204-06608.title: Modularity benefits reinforcement learning agents with competing homeostatic drives
arxiv-2204-06608.creator: Zack Dulberg, Rachit Dubey, Isabel M. Berwian, Jonathan D. Cohen
arxiv-2204-06608.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zack Dulberg, Rachit Dubey, Isabel M. Berwian, Jonathan D. Cohen. The problem of balancing conflicting needs is fundamental to intelligence. Standard reinforcement learning algorithms maximize a scalar reward, which requires combining different objective-specific rewards into a single number. Alternatively, different objectives could also be combined at the level of action value, such that specialist modules responsible for different objectives submit different action suggestions to a decision process, each based on rewards that are independent of one another.

arxiv-2208-07401.title: Algebraic Hyperbolicity of Complements of Generic Hypersurfaces in Projective Spaces
arxiv-2208-07401.creator: Xi Chen, Eric Riedl, Wern Yeong
arxiv-2208-07401.description: Abstract . We study the algebraic hyperbolicity of the complement of very general degree 2 ​ n 2n hypersurfaces in ℙ n {{\mathbb{P}}}^{n} . We prove the Algebraic Green-Griffiths-Lang Conjecture for these complements, and in the case of the complement of a quartic plane curve, we completely characterize the exceptional locus as the union of the flex and bitangent lines.

arxiv-2209-01187.title: Conformal Assouad dimension as the critical exponent for combinatorial modulus
arxiv-2209-01187.creator: Mathav Murugan
arxiv-2209-01187.description: Abstract The conformal Assouad dimension is the infimum of all possible values of Assouad dimension after a quasisymmetric change of metric. We show that the conformal Assouad dimension equals a critical exponent associated to the combinatorial modulus for any compact doubling metric space.

arxiv-2210-00397.title: Connecting XOR and XOR* games
arxiv-2210-00397.creator: Lorenzo Catani 1, Ricardo Faleiro 2, Pierre-Emmanuel Emeriau 3, Shane Mansfield 3, Anna Pappa 1
arxiv-2210-00397.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Catani 1, Ricardo Faleiro 2, Pierre-Emmanuel Emeriau 3, Shane Mansfield 3, Anna Pappa 1. In this work we focus on two classes of games: XOR nonlocal games and XOR* sequential games with monopartite resources. XOR games have been widely studied in the literature of nonlocal games, and we introduce XOR* games as their natural counterpart within the class of games where a resource system is subjected to a sequence of controlled operations and a final measurement.

arxiv-2302-07309.title: Augmenting Pathologists with NaviPath: Design and Evaluation of a Human-AI Collaborative Navigation System Conference: Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 23–28, 2023; Hamburg, Germany Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computin
arxiv-2302-07309.creator: Hongyan Gu, Chunxu Yang, Mohammad Haeri, Jing Wang, Shirley Tang, Wenzhong Yan, Shujin He, Christopher Kazu Williams, Shino Magaki, Xiang ‘Anthony’ Chen
arxiv-2302-07309.description: Abstract . Artificial Intelligence (AI) brings advancements to support pathologists in navigating high-resolution tumor images to search for pathology patterns of interest. However, existing AI-assisted tools have not realized this promised potential due to a lack of insight into pathology and HCI considerations for pathologists’ navigation workflows in practice.

arxiv-2306-08414.title: Role of negative-energy states on the E2-M1 polarizability of optical clocks
arxiv-2306-08414.creator: Fang-Fei Wu, Ting-Yun Shi, Wei-Tou Ni, and Li-Yan Tang †
arxiv-2306-08414.description: Abstract The theoretical calculations of the dynamic E2-M1 polarizability at the magic wavelength of the Sr optical clock are inconsistent with experimental results. We investigate role of negative-energy states in the E2 and M1 polarizabilities. Our result for E2-M1 polarizability difference − - 7.74(3.92) × \times 10 -5 a.u.

arxiv-2401-13322.title: Polynomial-free unisolvence of polyharmonic splines with odd exponent by random sampling
arxiv-2401-13322.creator: Alvise Sommariva, Marco Vianello
arxiv-2401-13322.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alvise Sommariva, Marco Vianello. In a recent paper almost sure unisolvence of RBF interpolation at random points with no polynomial addition was proved, for Thin-Plate Splines and Radial Powers with noninteger exponent. The proving technique left unsolved the case of odd exponents. In this short note we prove almost sure polynomial-free unisolvence in such instances, by a deeper analysis of the interpolation matrix determinant and fundamental properties of analytic functions. 2020 AMS subject classification: 65D05,65D12.

arxiv-2403-15465.title: Most Likely Sequence Generation for n n -Grams, Transformers, HMMs, and Markov Chains, by Using Rollout Algorithms This work was carried out at the Fulton School of Computing, and Augmented Intelligence, Arizona State University, Tempe, AZ.
arxiv-2403-15465.creator: Yuchao Li, Dimitri Bertsekas
arxiv-2403-15465.description: Abstract In this paper we consider a transformer with an n n -gram structure, such as the one underlying ChatGPT. The transformer provides next word probabilities, which can be used to generate word sequences. We consider methods for computing word sequences that are highly likely, based on these probabilities. Computing the optimal (i.e.

arxiv-2409-06364.title: What happens to diffusion model likelihood when your model is conditional?
arxiv-2409-06364.creator: Mattias Cross, Anton Ragni
arxiv-2409-06364.description: Abstract DM iteratively denoise random samples to produce high-quality data. The iterative sampling process is derived from SDE , allowing a speed-quality trade-off chosen at inference. Another advantage of sampling with differential equations is exact likelihood computation. These likelihoods have been used to rank unconditional DM s and for out-of-domain classification.

arxiv-2501-18779.title: Spectral Insights and Evolutionary Pathways of Globular Cluster ULX in NGC 1399: A Two-Decade X-ray and Optical Study
arxiv-2501-18779.creator: Kwangmin Oh, Kristen C. Dage, Alexey Bobrick, Elias Aydi, Arash Bahramian, Adelle J. Goodwin, Daryl Haggard, Jimmy Irwin, Arunav Kundu, Jay Strader, Thomas J. Maccarone, Stephen E. Zepf
arxiv-2501-18779.description: Abstract We present new multi-wavelength observations of two ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) hosted by globular clusters (GCs) in the giant elliptical NGC 1399, focusing on CXO J0338318-352604 (GCU7), only the second GC ULX known to have luminous optical emission lines. Notably, only [N ii ] and [O iii ] emission is observed in the optical spectra, suggesting H-poor material.

arxiv-2503-00228.title: Seeing Eye to AI? Applying Deep-Feature-Based Similarity Metrics to Information Visualization
arxiv-2503-00228.creator: Sheng Long, Angelos Chatzimparmpas, Emma Alexander, Matthew Kay, Jessica Hullman
arxiv-2503-00228.description: Abstract . Judging the similarity of visualizations is crucial to various applications, such as visualization-based search and visualization recommendation systems. Recent studies show deep-feature-based similarity metrics correlate well with perceptual judgments of image similarity and serve as effective loss functions for tasks like image super-resolution and style transfer. We explore the application of such metrics to judgments of visualization similarity.

arxiv-2505-20390.title: Nonperturbative Quantum Gravity in a Closed Lorentzian Universe
arxiv-2505-20390.creator: Yasunori Nomura
arxiv-2505-20390.description: Abstract We study how meaningful physical predictions can arise in nonperturbative quantum gravity in a closed Lorentzian universe. In such settings, recent developments suggest that the quantum gravitational Hilbert space is one-dimensional and real for each α \alpha -sector, as induced by spacetime wormholes.

arxiv-2510-07562.title: EBGAN-MDN: An Energy-Based Adversarial Framework for Multi-Modal Behavior Cloning
arxiv-2510-07562.creator: Yixiao Li, Julia Barth, Thomas Kiefer, Ahmad Fraij
arxiv-2510-07562.description: Abstract Multi-modal behavior cloning faces significant challenges due to mode averaging and mode collapse, where traditional models fail to capture diverse input-output mappings. This problem is critical in applications like robotics, where modeling multiple valid actions ensures both performance and safety. We propose EBGAN-MDN, a framework that integrates energy-based models, Mixture Density Networks (MDNs), and adversarial training.

arxiv-2511-05873.title: EndoIR: Degradation-Agnostic All-in-One Endoscopic Image Restoration via Noise-Aware Routing Diffusion
arxiv-2511-05873.creator: Tong Chen, Xinyu Ma, Long Bai, Wenyang Wang, Yue Sun, Luping Zhou
arxiv-2511-05873.description: Abstract Endoscopic images often suffer from diverse and co-occurring degradations such as low lighting, smoke, and bleeding, which obscure critical clinical details. Existing restoration methods are typically task-specific and often require prior knowledge of the degradation type, limiting their robustness in real-world clinical use.

arxiv-2601-20173.title: MAPLE: Self-supervised Learning-Enhanced Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction for Visual Analysis
arxiv-2601-20173.creator: Zeyang Huang, Takanori Fujiwara, Angelos Chatzimparmpas, Wandrille Duchemin, Andreas Kerren
arxiv-2601-20173.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Zeyang Huang, Takanori Fujiwara, Angelos Chatzimparmpas, Wandrille Duchemin, Andreas Kerren. We present a new nonlinear dimensionality reduction method, MAPLE , that enhances UMAP by improving manifold modeling. MAPLE employs a self-supervised learning approach to more efficiently encode low-dimensional manifold geometry. Central to this approach are maximum manifold capacity representations (MMCRs) , which help untangle complex manifolds by compressing variances among locally similar data points while amplifying variance among dissimilar data points.

pmc-10886127.title: A three-player game model for promoting enterprise green technology innovation from the perspective of media coverage
pmc-10886127.creator: Yan Liu, Yun-ping Chen, Tong-ping Xie, Yi-han Xia
pmc-10886127.description: ObjectiveThe objective of this study was to explore the game relationship among enterprise, the government, and the public under the new media environment, so as to provide decision-making reference for improving enterprise green technology innovation and promoting economy high-quality development with new media participation.

pmc-11359655.title: Chitosan-Coated Liposome Formulations for Encapsulation of Ciprofloxacin and Etoposide
pmc-11359655.creator: Rubén Gil-Gonzalo, D. Alonzo Durante-Salmerón, Saeedeh Pouri, Ernesto Doncel-Pérez, Andrés R. Alcántara, Inmaculada Aranaz, Niuris Acosta
pmc-11359655.description: Cancer and bacterial infections rank among the most significant global health threats. accounting for roughly 25 million fatalities each year. This statistic underscores the urgent necessity for developing novel drugs, enhancing current treatments, and implementing systems that boost their bioavailability to achieve superior therapeutic outcomes.

pmc-11477751.title: Fractional Talbot Lithography for Predesigned Large-Area Liquid-Crystal Alignment
pmc-11477751.creator: Zhichao Ji, Zenghua Gan, Yu Wang, Zhijian Liu, Donghao Yang, Yujie Fan, Wenhua Li, Irena Drevensek-Olenik, Yigang Li, Xinzheng Zhang
pmc-11477751.description: To address the increasing demands for cost-effective, large-area, and precisely patterned alignment of liquid crystals, a fractional Talbot lithography alignment technique was proposed. A light intensity distribution with a double spatial frequency of a photomask could be achieved based on the fractional Talbot effect, which not only enhanced the resolution of lithography but also slashed system costs with remarkable efficiency.

pmc-11508303.title: Pulmonary Embolism Management Audit and Machine Learning Analysis of Delayed Anticoagulation in a Swiss Teaching Hospital
pmc-11508303.creator: Cedrine Kueng, Maria Boesing, Stéphanie Giezendanner, Jörg Daniel Leuppi, Giorgia Lüthi-Corridori
pmc-11508303.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: Diagnosing acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is challenging due to its wide range of symptoms and numerous differential diagnoses. Medical professionals must balance performing all essential examinations and avoiding unnecessary testing. This study aimed to retrospectively audit the diagnosis and treatment of acute PE at a Swiss public teaching hospital to determine the adherence to current guidelines and to identify the factors associated with the delayed initiation of anticoagulation in PE patients.

pmc-11610299.title: Clinical trials in neuromodulatory treatment of drug-resistant hypertension and the need for spinal cord stimulation trials: a PRISMA systematic review
pmc-11610299.creator: Garrett W Thrash, Elijah Wang, Yifei Sun, Harrison C Walker, Prasad Shirvalkar, Bryan K Becker, Marshall T Holland
pmc-11610299.description: BackgroundDrug-resistant hypertension affects approximately 9–18% of the United States hypertensive population. Recognized as hypertension that is resistant to three or more medications, drug-resistant hypertension can lead to fatal sequelae, such as heart failure, aortic dissection, and other vast systemic disease. The disruption of the homeostatic mechanisms that stabilize blood pressure can be treated procedurally when medication fails.

pmc-11728035.title: Comparing the Efficacy of CT, MRI, PET-CT, and US in the Detection of Cervical Lymph Node Metastases in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma with Clinically Negative Neck Lymph Node: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11728035.creator: Ahmed Alsibani, Abdulwahed Alqahtani, Roaa Almohammadi, Tahera Islam, Mohammed Alessa, Saleh F Aldhahri, Khalid Hussain Al-Qahtani, Christos Sachpekidis
pmc-11728035.description: Background: Traditional imaging techniques have limited efficacy in detecting occult cervical lymph node (LN) metastases in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET-CT) has demonstrated potential for assessing HNSCC, but the literature on its efficacy for detecting cervical LN metastases is scarce and exhibits varied outcomes, hindering comparisons.

pmc-12182834.title: Intensive chemotherapy after hypomethylating agent and venetoclax in adult acute myeloid leukemia∗
pmc-12182834.creator: Kuo-Kai Chin, Yannis Valtis, Andriy Derkach, Meira Yisraeli Salman, Leora Boussi, Jenna Ciervo, Mark B. Geyer, Jae H. Park, Martin S. Tallman, Jacob L. Glass, Aaron D. Goldberg, Eytan M. Stein
pmc-12182834.description: Key Points•After HMA/VEN treatment, patients with AML treated with IC had a CR/CRi rate of 28% and mOS of 7.2 months.•Patients aged >65 years performed poorly with IC after HMA/VEN, achieving a mOS of 4.3 months (vs 10.6 months for younger patients).

pmc-12589611.title: Suppression of the Asian tiger mosquito (Aedes albopictus) populations using the boosted sterile insect technique in Greece
pmc-12589611.creator: Athanasios Giatropoulos, Georgios Balatsos, Vasileios Karras, Renaud Lancelot, Jérémy Bouyer, Arianna Puggioli, Romeo Bellini, Nikos T. Papadopoulos, Dimitrios P. Papachristos, Ioannis Mouratidis, Antonios Michaelakis
pmc-12589611.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The boosted Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) by releasing sterilized males coated with the larvicide pyriproxyfen has been suggested for the control of Aedes container-breeding mosquitoes. In 2023, a boosted-SIT field trial was applied in Greece against Aedes albopictus by weekly releases of pyriproxyfen-coated sterile males at the beginning (12 May–16 June) and peak (1 September–6 October) of mosquito activity, including two Mark-Release-Recapture sessions in July.

pmc-12641412.title: Changes in psychotropic medication prescription patterns during the COVID-19 pandemic among Japanese children, adolescents and young adults: interrupted time-series study using a national claims database
pmc-12641412.creator: Wenbo Huang, Hiroki Matsui, Yusuke Sasabuchi, Hideo Yasunaga
pmc-12641412.description: BackgroundTo date, no research has explored the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on psychotropic prescription patterns among young people in Japan, where lockdown measures were relatively less stringent.AimsThis study aimed to investigate changes in the prescription patterns of psychotropic medications for Japanese young people before and after the COVID-19 pandemic, using the DeSC Database.

pmc-13202984.title: Eagle syndrome causing cerebral infarction attributed to the synergistic effect of mild compression of the styloid process and carotid artery arteriosclerosis: a case report
pmc-13202984.creator: Taiki Tokuyama, Yuki Sakaeyama, Mitsuyoshi Abe, Shuhei Kubota, Chie Matsuura, Yutaka Fuchinoue, Sayaka Terazono, Nobuo Sugo
pmc-13202984.description: BackgroundCerebral infarction in Eagle syndrome is caused by blood flow disruption attributed to direct compression of the internal carotid artery by the styloid process. Herein, we report a rare case of Eagle syndrome in which mild compression of the styloid process and stylohyoid ligament caused tortuosity of the proximal internal carotid artery, leading to severe stenosis and cerebral infarction.

pmc-13383221.title: Comparative evaluation of intralesional platelet-rich plasma and triamcinolone in management of oral submucous fibrosis: A prospective clinical study
pmc-13383221.creator: Vipul Ughade, Sanyog Pathak, Sumit Asrani, Rajesh Dhirawani, Harshit Shrivastava
pmc-13383221.description: BackgroundOral Submucous Fibrosis (OSMF) is a chronic, progressive, potentially malignant disorder characterized by fibrosis of the oral mucosa, resulting in restricted mouth opening, burning sensation, mucosal blanching, and reduced cheek flexibility. Effective management remains challenging, and newer regenerative therapies such as platelet-rich plasma (PRP) have shown promising results.
